results.title: Delays in alternative petroleum discharge facility adding up to GH¢0.60 per litre in costs – CEMSE
results.content: The Centre for Media, Society and Economic Studies (CEMSE) says delays in developing alternative facilities for discharging petroleum products are contributing to higher costs in Ghana's downstream petroleum sector, with demurrage charges estimated to add between GH¢0.47 and GH¢0.60 to the cost of each litre of fuel. In a statement issued on Thursday, November 5, 2026, the think tank called for urgent investment in alternative petroleum discharge infrastructure, warning that Ghana's continued dependence on the major facility at Tema is exposing the sector to congestion, delays and additional costs. CEMSE said the sector recorded cumulative demurrage costs of approximately US$61.6 million in 2025, compared with a historical annual estimate of about US$35 million. results.title: Italian chef fired after refusing to put pineapple on pizza
results.content: An Italian chef sacked from a Brisbane restaurant had refused to put pineapple on a pizza because it was an "insult to his culture".

results.title: Ghanaians look back on Christmas memories that have stayed with them
results.content: From childhood surprises and a first trip abroad to simple family gatherings, some Ghanaians have Christmas memories that have remained special to them over the years. As part of our Christmas series, we spoke to people about the celebrations and experiences from their past that they still remember fondly. For Kate Quayeson, Christmas as a child was a time to look forward to new shoes, dresses and other treats from her mother. She recalled how her mother would use a broom to measure her legs before buying her Christmas shoes, often choosing a bigger size so she could wear them the following year. “My mother will use broom to measure my leg. Then she'll go and buy a shoe that is bigger than my size, maybe like for the next year or something,” she said.

results.title: Over 60,000 teachers complete GES promotion exercise as new policy expands career opportunities
results.content: More than 60,000 teachers across the country have completed the three-day Ghana Education Service (GES) promotion exercise, which is expected to significantly expand opportunities for career advancement under a policy that separates professional ranks from administrative positions.

results.title: JoyNews’ Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom shortlisted for 2026 AMDF Journalist of the Year Award
results.content: JoyNews’ Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom has been selected as a finalist for the 2026 Africa Media Development Foundation (AMDF) Journalist of the Year Award in the Television category. The selection recognises his contribution to journalism and follows what the Foundation describes as a highly competitive assessment of entries submitted for this year’s awards. In a congratulatory message to the journalist, the AMDF said his work stood out among the entries considered by the panel of judges. “We are delighted to recognise your contribution to journalism through this year's awards,” the Foundation stated.

results.title: Understaffing at AG’s office hindering prosecution of ORAL cases, recovery of state funds – Martin Kpebu
results.content: A former member of the Operation Recover All Loot (ORAL) Committee, Martin Kpebu, has blamed understaffing at the Attorney-General’s Department for the inability to effectively pursue cases identified by the committee and recover alleged stolen state funds.

results.title: GPL: Hearts of Oak’s Nebojsa, and two others nominated for Coach of the Month award
results.content: Hearts of Oak head coach Nebojsa Kapor, Swedru All Blacks trainer Joseph Agyeman, and Medeama SC coach Tanko Ibrahim are the three contenders, having each guided their teams to three victories in four matches.

results.title: CPS to award best-performing student in Economics at UG City Campus
results.content: The Centre for Policy Scrutiny (CPS) has announced plans to award the best-performing Economics student at the University of Ghana to promote academic excellence and encourage outstanding performance among students.

results.title: Jinapor calls for Africa to develop solar value chain to boost energy security
results.content: The Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Jinapor, has called on African countries to harness their solar energy potential to strengthen energy security, reduce dependence on imported fuels and drive industrialisation.

results.title: IMF flags delayed ECG collection accounts audit, urges timely reforms
results.content: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has flagged Ghana’s delayed publication of an audit of the Electricity Company of Ghana’s collection accounts. It urged the government to complete outstanding reforms on time.

results.title: Over 100 golfers to participate in GCB Opemsuo Invitational Golf Tournament in Kumasi
results.content: GCB Bank is partnering the Royal Golf Club Kumasi to organize the one day 18-hole golf competition on 28th November 2026, to celebrate the rich Asante royal heritage and bring together business leaders and golf enthusiasts on one stage.

results.title: Martin Kpebu says ORAL did not agree on $21.19bn state asset recovery estimate
results.content: A former member of the Operation Recover All Loot (ORAL) Committee, Martin Kpebu, has disputed claims that the government could recover up to $21.19 billion from stolen state assets.

results.title: IMF gives Ghana’s economic recovery a strong endorsement
results.content: The International Monetary Fund has strongly endorsed Ghana’s economic recovery, citing robust growth, low inflation, and stronger public finances.

results.title: Ghana meets most PCI targets, but risks remain – IMF
results.content: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has described Ghana’s performance under its Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI) programme as broadly satisfactory, with most quantitative targets met.

results.title: Ghana adds 500,000 to 700,000 people to its population annually – Statistician
results.content: Ghana’s population is increasing by an estimated 500,000 to 700,000 people annually, with the country’s total population currently standing at approximately 33.7 million, Government Statistician Dr Alhassan Iddrisu has disclosed.

results.title: Falling reserves force changes to Ghana’s gold and forex arrangements – IMF
results.content: Falling foreign exchange reserves have prompted Ghana to shift forex intermediation from the Bank of Ghana to GoldBod and require large-scale miners to sell more gold.

results.title: 92% of Ghanaian households have access to improved drinking water – Government Statistician
results.content: About 92 per cent of households in Ghana have access to improved drinking water, representing a significant increase from 60.7 per cent recorded in 2000, Government Statistician Dr Alhassan Iddrisu has disclosed.

results.title: UNFPA urges Ghana to make population data central to national development planning
results.content: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) has called on Ghana to place population data and demographic trends at the centre of its national development planning to support evidence-based policies and sustainable economic growth.

results.title: UNFPA urges stronger partnerships to end maternal deaths, child marriage and gender-based violence in Ghana
results.content: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) has called for stronger partnerships among government institutions, traditional authorities, civil society organisations and development partners to accelerate efforts to end preventable maternal deaths, child marriage and gender-based violence in Ghana.

results.title: Ghana’s population growth rate drops to 2.1%, population to double in 33 years – Gov’t Statistician
results.content: Ghana’s annual population growth rate has declined to 2.1 per cent, extending the period within which the country’s population is expected to double to approximately 33 years, Government Statistician Dr Alhassan Iddrisu has said.
